focus.jtag: Renewed U.S.–Iran diplomatic efforts keep oil choppy near a 6-month high, futures firm ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision, and a monster earnings week rolls on. The scanner boarded WHR, XYL, CLS (Type A), PG and BUG (Type C)
focus.jnote: The environment is stabilizing but far from clear. U.S. stock futures rose early Tuesday after Wall Street closed higher in the previous session, lifted by AI optimism following Anthropic's IPO filing. Wall Street closed higher Monday to start the final week of a volatile October, with the S&P up 0.70% to ~7,677 and all three major indexes finishing positive. Oil is choppy: crude prices inched higher Tuesday, reversing earlier losses driven by renewed diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.–Iran war and hopes of a de-escalation in the wider regional conflict. Brent fell to ~$115.23 on October 27, down 0.50% from the prior day, but is still up ~18% over the past month. Volatility has eased slightly — the VIX fell 5.5% Monday to 18.39 and sits near 19 this morning. This is a Fed-decision week with an unresolved oil tail — not a clean premium-selling backdrop.
focus.notdown: The boarded bullish names split cleanly. The cleanest is PG (Type C, A+) — a fiscal-Q1 earnings beat pushed P&G to a fresh 52-week high of $165.59, clearing its February peak after eight months of sideways drift. The scanner's $159.35 pivot has held 2 sessions on 2.47x volume, a stronger structure than a same-day pop. CLS (Type A, B+) is a blowout double-beat — Q3 revenue jumped 83% to $5.83 billion and adjusted EPS more than doubled to $3.30 — gapping ~12–17% premarket, but the scanner flags thin liquidity (OI 42, unverified ATM). BUG (Type C, B+) is a same-day breakout near its $50.58 52-week high with unknown next-earnings. Watch-only on a RED, Fed-week day.
focus.notup: Two bearish Type A names boarded — WHR and XYL — both clean guidance-cut misses. Whirlpool reported an adjusted loss of 21 cents versus an ~80-cent consensus and slashed full-year guidance to a loss of $1.30 per share. Xylem's five-quarter beat streak ended and management cut full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $5.40–$5.45 from $5.55–$5.70 on project delays. Both gapped down hard. But selling bear calls into a VIX-near-19, FOMC-decision tape invites a squeeze on any dovish-Fed or de-escalation headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~60 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at ~41% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. On top of that, the Federal Reserve began its two-day policy meeting with the rate decision landing Wednesday 10/28, inside any normal DTE — an automatic stand-down trigger. The boarded names include genuinely clean setups (PG especially), but a live Fed decision plus an oil tail is not a tape to underwrite new premium into. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past Wednesday and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: FOMC decision · Wed 10/28 — the Federal Reserve began its two-day policy meeting with the rate call landing Wednesday. A hawkish surprise inside any normal DTE is the week's number-one scheduled gap risk — keep every spread clear of Wednesday.
ECB (Thu) & BoJ (Fri) — a back-to-back central-bank gauntlet follows the Fed, with the RBNZ, BoC and Fed on Wednesday. These can whipsaw rates, the dollar and risk all week.

Oil & Strait of Hormuz — security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey were set to meet Iranian leaders to revive talks, and Hormuz shipments have recovered toward prewar levels even as Brent holds near a six-month high. Any shipping incident sends crude vertical again — the biggest open-ended tail.

Mega-cap AI earnings · Wed 10/28 — Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday, the same day as the Fed. A disappointing hyperscaler print stacked on the rate decision is a double catalyst that could re-crack the whole index.

Thin / unconfirmed boarded setups — CLS has unverified liquidity and OI of just 42; WHR and XYL gapped on near-zero relative volume (0.08x and 0.01x); BUG is a same-day breakout with an unknown earnings date. Treat all five as watch-only, not tradeable spreads, on a RED day.
